votes.question: On Passage — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. This vote would have replaced that bill with a broader ban that also forces members, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children to sell covered investments they already hold. A Yea would have made that swap; a Nay kept the original bill.

votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: The fiscal year 2027 defense bill sets military policy, troop levels, and related Energy Department security programs. votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have required the Defense Secretary to report options for cutting the department's civilian workforce by 200,000. A Yea would have added that report. A Nay voted not to add it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)

votes.plain_language: This amendment to the fiscal year 2027 defense bill would ban automated speed-enforcement cameras on military bases. A Yea adds that ban to the bill. A Nay leaves the bill without it.

A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

posts.text: Happy Veterans Day to all my fellow veterans across Montana. Montana serves at one of the highest percentages in the country. We are proud to call so many veterans our friends and neighbors. To all who have worn our nation’s uniform, thank you for serving our country. https://t.co/SXFEzSPRri

Happy 251st birthday to the United States Marine Corps. To every Marine in Montana and across the country who has earned the Eagle, Globe, and Anchor, thank you for answering the call and defending our freedom. Semper Fi! https://t.co/nebFsJ3tS9

Lola and I are heartbroken by the loss of Lincoln County Deputy Ryan Terpsma, who was killed while protecting his community and doing his duty. We are praying for his family and fellow officers, and for the families of those who were killed or injured during this incident. May God bring comfort and strength to everyone affected by this tragedy.

Happy opening day Montana! Good luck to everyone heading out for rifle season. Hunting is part of who we are, and protecting our public lands allows us to pass that tradition on to our kids. Hunt safe and fill those freezers.
Always great to start the morning at Montana Coffee. Good coffee, great conversations, and this morning, an extra blessing with a prayer to start the day. https://t.co/uJDvCIcOsp

Congratulations to Travis Naugle and Silver Bow Mining for making Montana a Treasure State Again. The acquisition of the troubled Montana Tunnels fully restored full state bonding and will honor more than four million dollars of tax debt to Jefferson County Schools. Good news for America’s critical mineral supply chain and great news for high paying Montana jobs. Bravo Zulu!

In a recent survey conducted by my office, 87% of respondents said Congress should reduce the tax burden on working families. I'll always fight to protect access and support the communities that depend on our parks. Glacier is my home and it is my mission to protect it for Montana.

250 years ago, our Founding Fathers risked everything to give birth to the greatest nation the world has ever known. Today, 250 years later, America stands stronger than ever as history’s greatest champion of freedom.

May God bless the United States of America and all those who defend her.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
